crime_highlights: Mr. Abdi and another man were observed moving about the black BMW
When the second man was seen handling a gun, the police were called.
Police later seized a revolver from the rear footwell of the white BMW.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Abdi’s personal circumstances were clearly considered to contextualize his criminal record.
It is mitigating that the Defendant has had a difficult personal history as a first generation Canadian who is a member of a visible minority.
This explains, in part, how the Defendant has ended up before the courts on a number of occasions.
The sentencing judge appreciated the significance of Mr. Abdi’s personal circumstances in assessing his moral blameworthiness
He clearly considered the IRCA to contextualize Mr. Abdi’s culpability for a serious offence.
note: Appeal court describes trial judge's use of IRCA; no harm to victims, firearm offence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Knockwood ended the altercation once he had the weapon, by stabbing Troy a couple of times in the leg.
Mr. Knockwood then continues punching Mr. Whidden and hits Mr. Whidden with the blunt end of the bayonet to ensure he is knocked out.
The stabbing inflicted by the appellant to Mr. Whidden’s rear left leg/lower buttock perforated the femoral vein and caused Mr. Whidden to bleed to death.
rationale_highlights: The Gladue Report speaks powerfully to the issues that must be considered in determining Nathan Knockwood's moral culpability.
it would be impossible to deny the profoundly significant direct connection between his experience as a Mi'kmaq man in Nova Scotia and the circumstances of this case.
Both speak to Mr. Knockwood's moral blameworthiness or moral culpability.
while acknowledging the impacts of Mr. Knockwood's background and heritage on his moral culpability
note: Sentencing judge's reasons; appeal court later found he failed to explain effect.

crime_highlights: He was also convicted of possessing a loaded .32 calibre handgun and ammunition while conducting his violent and socially destructive trade.
The three were arrested and a search of the vehicle turned up the loaded .32 Smith and Weston, with extra ammunition for that gun, 17.5 grams of cocaine

The judge determined that Mr. White and his brother were conducting a cocaine and cannabis trafficking enterprise which preceded his arrest and would have continued but for his apprehension by police.
The guns were to protect themselves and their enterprise.
rationale_highlights: He fully appreciated the systemic and background factors that contributed to Mr. White coming into conflict with the law.
including consideration of Mr. White’s personal circumstances as described in his IRCA reports
Mr. White’s culpability viewed through the lens of his personal circumstances.
Both the seriousness of the offence and Mr. White’s moral culpability call for a carceral sentence of 4 years.
note: Crown appeal; court describes trial judge's IRCA use, then substitutes 4 years.
